actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The README describes heterogeneous multi-robot autonomy on Unitree Go2W (wheeled-legged) and Go2 (walking) quadrupeds with ROS 2 Humble, a MuJoCo simulation and a native ROS 1 Noetic deployment on the real Go2's Jetson Orin NX.
The README architecture diagram starts from 'MuJoCo ops2 (500 Hz)' or a real or HIL Mid-360 LiDAR, followed by mujoco_sensor_bridge or livox_ros_driver2.
The README lists 'mujoco_ros2_control/' as the DFKI MuJoCo ros2_control hardware interface.
The VLM MuJoCo launch defaults mujoco_model_path to go2_gazebo_sim/mujoco/vlm_exploration_scene.xml when the argument is empty.
The base MuJoCo launch starts the mujoco_ros2_control node with robot_model_path set to the selected MJCF, simulation_frequency 500.0 and real_time_factor 1.0.
The scene is an MJCF model named vlm_exploration_scene that compiles angles in radians and resolves mesh files from the assets directory.
The scene sets option timestep 0.002 s, gravity 0 0 -9.81, the implicitfast integrator and elliptic friction cones.
The Go2W base body starts at pos 4.0 0 0.6 and carries a free joint named root.
The base body carries the free joint root and each of the four legs carries hip, thigh, calf and foot joints, 16 named leg and foot joints in total.
The go2 default class sets the motor ctrlrange to -23.7 23.7, the knee class overrides it to -45.43 45.43, and the abduction/front_hip/back_hip/knee classes bound the leg joint ranges.
The actuator block has 12 motor actuators on the leg joints and four velocity actuators on the foot joints; each velocity actuator declares ctrlrange -15 15.
The scene declares accelerometer, gyro, foot touch and base frame sensors.
The knee default class sets the joint range -2.7227 -0.83776.
The README's License section says: 'Research project. Contact maintainers for licensing.'
The go2_gazebo_sim package manifest declares the MIT licence.

determinism.notes: Event-driven placeholder integration with no contact, constraint or force solver; the same control input reproduces the same placeholder state hash, but this is a stand-in digest, not a MuJoCo trajectory or state-hash replay.

gaps: the fake is a package-local stand-in for the mujoco module: it parses the MJCF and its includes for model shape, actuator names and ctrlranges, but it loads no meshes, textures, inertias or contacts and runs no MuJoCo physics

each actuator's force (gear * ctrl for the 12 motors, kv * (ctrl - qvel) for the four velocity actuators) accelerates only its own joint against a placeholder unit inertia, with a placeholder damping on the motor joints; the free base, gravity, contacts, friction, joint limits, force limits and sensor physics are not integrated (model review 2026-11-05: it used to treat every control value as a joint velocity)
reset restores qpos0 from the MJCF (base pos 4.0 0 0.6, identity quaternion, joints at their ref of 0) as mj_resetData does; it used to zero every qpos entry, including the quaternion
the snapshot uses the bridge's basic profile (time, qpos, qvel, act and ctrl) because the stand-in exposes no full integration-state API; warm-start and derived quantities are not preserved
the upstream ROS 2 graph, mujoco_ros2_control, the controllers, the sensor bridges, Nav2, SLAM and rendering are NOT COVERED
the published timestep_ms is read from the model's option element, but the fake's state advance is a placeholder and does not establish MuJoCo timing or determinism

safe_state.description: The simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no cap.world.step.v1 or cap.world.reset.v1 call is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, while the integration state stays readable.
